idiom_name: Ktor + JVM template engine (Thymeleaf/FreeMarker/Mustache) or the kotlinx.html DSL
implementation_notes: Kotlin has no page-template syntax of its own beyond string templates ("$name"), so server-side rendering goes through the framework: install the engine feature (install(Thymeleaf) { setTemplateResolver(...) }) and answer with call.respondTemplate("orders.html", model), using the same JVM engines the rest of the stack uses and Kotlin data classes as the model. The Kotlin-native alternative is kotlinx.html, a type-safe DSL that builds markup with functions (call.respondHtml { table { ... } }); that is a programmatic view rather than a template artifact, so pick it when compile-time checking matters more than designer-editable templates.
pitfalls: Kotlin string templates ("$row.name") look like templating but escape nothing; they are glue code, not an HTML page mechanism.
JVM engines resolve ${...} paths at runtime, so a renamed data-class property renders as an empty cell instead of failing the build.
Template resolvers and caches are shared and configured once: wiring them per request duplicates work and can produce inconsistent caches.
